LE17.evidence_summary: The Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae identifies Zmꜣ-Bḥd.t as the 17th Diospolite nome of Lower Egypt and Behdet/Tell el-Balamun as its capital. The University of Chicago/ISAC dissertation The Behdetite explicitly devotes a chapter to the cult of Horus the Behdetite at the two cities named Behdet: Edfu and Tell el-Balamun, establishing Tell el-Balamun as a genuine northern Behdet node in the god's cult history.
LE17.later_cult_note: UCL archaeological evidence emphasizes a major Amun temple complex at Semabehdet in Dynasties 26 and 30; therefore Horus-Behdetite and Amun layers must be period-separated rather than treated as mutually exclusive.
LE17.name_translation_boundary: Popular tables gloss the nome/symbol as 'the throne'. The stronger linguistic sources checked here verify the place-name and nome identity but do not by themselves establish the exact Russian translation 'Объединение трона'; retain that wording as UNVERIFIED_ETYMOGRAPHIC_GLOSS pending a dedicated lexical pass.

LE18.period_boundary: UCL notes that territory later forming nome 18 had earlier belonged to nome 13, so 16->17->18 is a valid standard later administrative ordering but not a timeless sequence for all periods.

transception_interpretation.operator: BACK -> FORWARD -> LEFT -> RIGHT -> FORWARD -> BACK
transception_interpretation.result: The left probe is no longer merely a popular-culture association: a scholarly Horus-Behdetite cult link to Tell el-Balamun exists. The right probe remains securely Bastet/Bubastis. What is still missing is a primary ritual/relic text that makes 16->17->18 a processional or theological sequence rather than an administrative adjacency.

why: LE16 Mendes is independently an Osirian phallus+backbone relic node.
Banebdjedet carries an Osiris-ba theological identity at Mendes.
The immediately following LE17 is a genuine northern Behdet node with an academically documented Horus-Behdetite cult history.
The immediately following LE18 is Bubastis/Bastet.
The sequence therefore has real geographical and cultic content on all three nodes even though a ritual 16->17->18 script is not yet demonstrated.
mendes_strengthening.important_nonclaim: Administrative adjacency plus cultic relevance does not by itself prove that Egyptian priests encoded an Osiris->Horus->Bastet ritual progression in nome numbering.
